title: Medical-grade Sterilizable Target for Fluid-immersed Fetoscope Optical Distortion Calibration
protocol: Prepare a 316 stainless steel sheet with a 1.2-mm thickness.
Draw a 40 mm x 40 mm square onto the sheet.
Cut the drawn square using a manual metal cutter.
Round the corners and sides of the sample using a file.
Place the cut sheet on a straight wooden or metal block slightly larger in size than the stainless steel sheet.
Position the assembly in the internal blast chamber.
Tightly seal the internal blast chamber to prevent sand from spreading.
Wear safety goggles to protect the eyes.
Position a blast gun perpendicular to and at least 4-5 cm away from the metal surface.
Apply the foot control for sandblasting.
Hold the sample tightly by the edge of the piece of wood or using another vice during sandblasting.
Repeat the sandblasting on the other side if both sides need the calibration pattern engraved.
Design a pattern of asymmetric circles.
Prepare a drawing exchange format (DXF) file of the design either using CAD software or another suitable programming language.
Place the calibration target in a sterile fluid container, such as a gallipot.
Fill the container with the target fluid or a similar sterile substance.
Adjust the zoom and sharpness of the endoscope as desired.
Immerse the endoscope in the fluid and hold it at a distance from the calibration target similar to the distance from the anatomy that the endoscope will later be used at.
Launch the calibration application and start the camera acquisition.
Move the tip of the endoscope slightly for different views while keeping the whole calibration pattern in view of the camera.
Keep the elliptical legend around the calibration pattern within the circular view of the endoscope.
Acquire at least 10 endoscopic camera views required for calibration.
Press the calibration key to start the calibration process using the images acquired so far.
Press the indicated calibration key to save the resulting calibration parameters in a YAML file.
Group the calibration parameters into the camera matrix and distortion coefficients.
